subject: science
skillName: Reducing the Impacts of Natural Hazards

items.prompt:
Which is a natural Earth process that can be a hazard?
A) An earthquake
B) A drawing
C) A quiet day
D) A color

Can people stop an earthquake from happening?
A) Yes, easily
B) No, but they can reduce its impact
C) Yes, with signs
D) No, and nothing can be done
items.answer: B) No, but they can reduce its impact

steps: People cannot stop earthquakes but can reduce harm.

items.prompt:
One solution to reduce flood damage is to
A) build a levee or wall
B) ignore the river
C) remove all warnings
D) build lower
items.answer: A) build a levee or wall

items.prompt:
A warning system helps during a hazard by
A) stopping the hazard
B) letting people get to safety in time
C) making the hazard bigger
D) doing nothing
items.answer: B) letting people get to safety in time

steps: Warnings give people time to reach safety.

items.prompt:
Why generate more than one solution for a hazard?
A) To waste time
B) To compare them and choose the best
C) To confuse people
D) There is no reason
items.answer: B) To compare them and choose the best

steps: Comparing solutions helps pick the most effective one.

items.prompt:
Stronger, earthquake-resistant buildings help by
A) stopping earthquakes
B) being less likely to collapse on people
C) warning people
D) making more quakes
items.answer: B) being less likely to collapse on people

steps: Stronger buildings protect the people inside.

items.prompt:
For earthquakes, which better reduces harm: warning signs alone, or stronger buildings?
A) Warning signs alone
B) Stronger buildings
C) They are equal
D) Neither helps

steps: Signs alone do not stop collapses, but stronger buildings do.

items.prompt:
Besides protecting people, a good hazard solution should fit the
A) available materials, time, and cost
B) color of the town
C) names of the engineers
D) weather report
items.answer: A) available materials, time, and cost

steps: Solutions must work within the constraints of materials, time, and cost.
